findings.text: Provides a cross-CPU invalidation request that forwards a caller supplied mask and descriptor to the native multi flush implementation selected by a compile time alias.

Performs address space switch on the current CPU with interrupts already disabled, updating loaded space and identifier, refreshing protection keys, segment tables and masking state, and choosing whether a full reload is required.

Handles an incoming shootdown on each target CPU by validating the loaded space, adopting a newly assigned broadcast identifier when needed, ignoring work already covered by broadcast or generation checks, and otherwise applying either a ranged or a full local invalidation before advancing the local generation.
A per address space generation is advanced atomically on every paging change and acts as a full barrier so paging writes are ordered before later observation of CPU membership by the switch path.

Hardware PCID values derive from small dynamic identifiers by adding one to avoid zero, while the user variant additionally sets the isolation switch bit when that mitigation is configured, with build and runtime checks keeping dynamic space clear of the switch bit.

An identifier counts as broadcast when outside the dynamic range, such identifiers stay current through hardware broadcast and cause early return in both shootdown handling and context switch fast paths, and a reload is needed when an address space owns a broadcast value different from the locally loaded one.

An address space starts without broadcast identifier, becomes transitioning when a value is assigned, stays there while remote CPUs still run with older values, receives an extra shootdown to prod stragglers, and leaves the state once every active CPU is observed using the new value.

Broadcast identifiers are drawn from a bitmap searched forward from the last grant, availability is counted down on grant, and reaching the end of space triggers a full nonglobal broadcast that permits recycling values marked as released and restarting allocation scanning at the first dynamic slot.

Assignment marks transition before publishing the new broadcast value with release ordering so a ranged flush that observes the value also observes the transition request and can complete the handover.

The global identifier bitmaps, last grant position and availability count are serialized by a single lock taken with interrupts saved in the promotion path and required held in allocation and space reset paths.

Promotion to broadcast invalidation is considered only when the broadcast capability is present, is sampled infrequently by comparing low bits of process number and timer tick, and proceeds only when the address space is simultaneously active beyond a small threshold.

Activity estimation first rejects sparsely shared spaces by mask population and then precisely counts CPUs whose loaded space matches and that are not in lazy mode, succeeding once the count passes the threshold.

Broadcast invalidation handles whole space and ranged requests separately, splits ranges into hardware limited batches with large page awareness, issues kernel and when needed user variants without waiting per operation, completes any identifier transition, then waits once for all broadcasts to finish.

Context switch publishes a switching marker with release semantics then enforces a barrier before reading the generation, which pairs with the generation bump and marker read on the flush side so either the switch sees the new generation or the flush sees the new membership.
If no broadcast value remains or allocation fails, promotion warns once and leaves the address space on the unicast shootdown path rather than blocking or reusing a live value.

The shootdown handler assumes interrupts disabled and nonreentrant execution, and the transition completion path polls CPUs reporting a switching marker with a relaxed wait to avoid acting on a stale loaded value during a concurrent switch.

Observed state comprises per address space generation, context identifier, broadcast value and transition flag, plus per-CPU loaded space pointer, loaded identifier, masking value, lazy flag, and per identifier slots holding context identifier and caught-up generation.

Behavior is keyed on symbolic limits and selectors including maximum and dynamic identifier counts, full flush and invalid generation sentinels, page size shifts, broadcast capability and isolation feature keys, isolation switch bit position, masking shift, and broadcast mode and flag selectors for PCID, address, stride and nonglobal scope.
A full nonglobal broadcast plus its completion wait executes under a preemption guard so the sequence cannot migrate CPUs midway.

Masking state is kept per CPU in compact form and expanded to control register mask form by shift, with empty variants when unsupported, and control register values combine the encrypted page table base with masking bits and the derived PCID when that feature is enabled.
When broadcast invalidation support is compiled out, assignment and clearing become no operations and the transition query constantly reports false, keeping all spaces on the unicast path.

A remote handler performs ranged invalidation only when the request is ranged and its target generation is exactly one past the local value and equals the current shared generation; any other stale case uses a full local flush, after which the local generation advances to the shared value.

A shootdown received on a CPU whose loaded space differs clears that CPU from the target mask and returns, the initial kernel space needs no action, and a CPU in lazy mode switches to the initial space instead of flushing, with tracing distinguishing local, remote and wrong CPU cases.

Switching to the same space can return early for broadcast identifiers or up to date non-lazy state and otherwise revalidates generation after a barrier, while switching spaces publishes membership, reads generation, selects a fresh identifier, loads the new page table base with masking, then publishes loaded state after a compiler barrier.
